_meta.description: Cumulative probability that a Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC) exists by a given year, 2026–2046.
sources: Global Risk Institute — Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025 (https://globalriskinstitute.org/publication/quantum-threat-timeline-report-2025b/) — expert survey (26 respondents): 28-49% probability within 10 years (by 2035), 51-70% within 15 years (by 2040), 92% of respondents ≥50% within 20 years (by 2045), ~50% call 20-year arrival 'extremely likely' (>99%)
_meta.methodology: Values at 2026, 2035, 2040 and 2045 are anchored to the GRI 2025 survey ranges above (low end of each range = 'slow' scenario, high end = 'fast' scenario). All other years are LINEARLY INTERPOLATED between those anchors — this curve is not itself a GRI-published series, only the four anchor points are. 2046 repeats the 2045 value (no anchor beyond 20 years).

scenarios.slow: Lower bound of each GRI 2025 survey range — a more conservative view of quantum computing progress.
scenarios.fast: Upper bound of each GRI 2025 survey range — a more aggressive view of quantum computing progress.
scenarios.consensus: Computed as the midpoint of slow and fast at each year (not independently sourced — see breachCostModel.ts crqcProbabilityAt()).

_meta.note: Educational model — probabilities represent one expert survey's aggregated estimates, not certified actuarial or scientific predictions of when a CRQC will exist.
_meta.supersedes: Previously anchored to GRI 2023 (optimistic/pessimistic keys); refreshed 2026-07 to GRI 2025. Key names 'optimistic'/'pessimistic' kept for backward compatibility with existing consumers — 'optimistic' now maps to the 'slow' CRQC scenario (best case for defenders), 'pessimistic' to 'fast'.
